First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡((2n-1)x).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=0,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡((2n-1)\cdot 0)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=1.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=0,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(0)=0.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡((2n-1)\cdot 0) \\ 0 & =\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot 1 \\ -\frac{\pi }{2} & =-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}} & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-2x+1, & x\in [-4,0] \\ {x}^{2}+2, & x\in (0,4)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the function $F(x)$ shown above. Find the value to which the Fourier series of the $8$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is converging when $x=-3.$

The Fourier series converges to {{field-1}} when $x=-3.$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is a $2L$-periodic piecewise smooth function with the corresponding Fourier series

$$
S(x)=\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x).
$$

Then, the series converges for all $x\in R.$

- If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x,$ then the series converges to the value of the function at this point:

$$
S(x)=f(x)
$$

- If $f(x)$ has a jump discontinuity at $x,$ then the series converges to the midpoint between the values of left- and right-sided limits of the function at this point:

$$
S(x)=\frac{{f}^{-}(x)+{f}^{+}(x)}{2}
$$

where ${f}^{-}(x)$ and ${f}^{+}(x)$ are the left- and right-sided limits of the function at this point, respectively.

Notice that the $8$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of our function $F(x)$ is continuous at $x=-3.$ 

Therefore, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ converges to 

$$
f(-3)=-2(-3)+1=7.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼-1+\frac{12}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,((2n-1)x).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=-\frac{\pi }{2},$ we have

$$
sin\,((2n-1)\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2}))=sin\,(\frac{\pi }{2}-n\pi )=(-1)^{n}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=-\frac{\pi }{2},$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(-\frac{\pi }{2})=-4.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$

$$
